Chapter 11: The Nature of Evil, Suffering, and Free Will
The world can feel harsh and unpredictable, can’t it? Every day, there’s news of violence, injustice, and suffering—sometimes it’s enough to make you wonder, why does this even happen?
In the safety of their circle, the group brought these big questions to Seth, hoping for some understanding, maybe even a little comfort.
Seth’s answer? It was both challenging and full of compassion. He said that what we usually call “evil” isn’t some force lurking out there—it’s actually a distortion of creative energy. Think about that for a second. Each soul is free to choose, and that freedom means there’s always a chance for mistakes, pain, or even cruelty. But here’s the thing—nothing is ever truly wasted. Even the darkest experiences can help us grow and understand ourselves better.
One young man, who’d seen violence in his own community, really struggled to accept this. How could suffering possibly have any purpose? Seth encouraged him to look a little deeper. Not to excuse or justify anyone’s pain, but to see that every soul is on its own journey, learning in its own way. Sometimes, those lessons are hard. And yes, the consequences are very real. But the soul? It’s always searching for balance, always reaching for greater understanding.
Seth described free will as both the greatest gift and the greatest challenge we have. Each of us gets to create our own reality—to choose love or fear, kindness or cruelty. The world, with all its beauty and all its pain, is really a tapestry woven from all those choices, coming together in a way that’s uniquely ours.
A woman in the group, who’d suffered betrayal, found real comfort in this idea. She realized she could choose how to respond. Forgiveness, she discovered, wasn’t about letting anyone off the hook. It was about freeing herself from the weight of the past. By choosing compassion, she found a new sense of peace she hadn’t known before.
Seth never claimed to have easy answers. He didn’t deny that suffering is real. But he invited everyone to see every experience—even the tough ones—as a chance to grow. To trust in the soul’s deep resilience. And to remember that, even in our darkest moments, there’s always hope.
As these sessions went on, the group grew more compassionate. They became more willing to face their own shadows, more able to find meaning in everything they experienced. The teachings encouraged them to honor their own choices, respect the choices of others, and, above all, trust in the ultimate goodness at the heart of every soul.
